title: Bootstrap samples takeaways & action log
body:
Attendees: Ava, Marco, Riley, Samira, Jonah
Date: 2026-11-18 standup-style sync (compact)
Context: short retro on the recent "bootstrap samples" pilot we shipped to the playground (10 example apps + 5 notebooks). Observations below – trying to capture concrete wins, friction, and follow-ups before we update the quickstart page.

Top-level summary:
- Win: onboarding time dropped for new signups who tried the 'chat-sdk-quickstart' from ~18m -> ~8m (self-reported + telemetry sample). People who used the notebook variant completed an example flow more often.
- Friction: multiple samples rely on an older auth flow (legacy token header) which caused two confusing failures for users on private deployments.
- Product gap: the samples don't surface token-cost estimates or guidance for batch vs streaming. New teams are asking for rules-of-thumb.

Detailed notes / snippets (choppy as promised):
- Marco: ran 30 user replays from the playground, 7% of runs hit a token-limit error; mostly due to example prompts with long context + streaming mode toggled off. Suggest adding a small note under each sample: "best for low-latency chat -> enable streaming".
- Riley: doc patch needed — examples/chat/long-context.md needs trimming + counterexamples. Also found a broken link to the model-compatibility table (points at an older Confluence anchor).
- Samira: UX flow in the notebook sample is too prescriptive (hard-coded batch_size=8). For small demo infra (free-tier), it OOMs. Proposed: detect env and pick safer defaults (batch_size=1, max_seq=512) + show a tooltip: "Change defaults for production workloads".
- Jonah: telemetry shows users who open the 'embedding quickstart' rarely run the evaluation cell. Hypothesis: notebook is too long / scattered. Action: create a 2-cell "instant win" embedding demo that returns a similarity score in <30s.

Bugs / regressions found:
- Auth mismatch on private deployments: samples use Authorization: Bearer <KEY> but our private SDK packages expect X-Redwood-Token in some older helper wrappers. Root cause: sample templates grabbed from repo commit b1c3f (pre-auth-consolidation).
- Two samples crash when run with py3.11 + the devexp venv: dependency pin missing for tokenizers==0.14. Suggested quick fix: pin in requirements.txt and add a CI smoke test against 3.11.

Decisions / mini-PRD notes (quick):
- Short-term (1 sprint):
  * Update samples: switch auth helper to unified get_redwood_token() wrapper across all examples. (owner: Marco)
  * Create "2-cell embedding" notebook and add to samples index. (owner: Jonah)
  * Add streaming hint line to chat samples and reduce long-context default. (owner: Riley)
  * Pin tokenizers and add 3.11 smoke. (owner: Samira)
- Medium-term (2-3 sprints):
  * Add token-cost estimator snippet per sample (small JS/Py function showing approximate token count + cost for local run). Keep it optional. (owner: Ava)
  * Add a lightweight QA checklist for samples before release: auth path, python versions (3.10/3.11), model-compatibility footers, CI smoke-pass.

Action items (explicit):
- Marco: PR to replace legacy auth helpers in examples/ (due 2026-11-24). Link PR to ENG-4921.
- Jonah: prototype 2-cell embedding notebook + add TOC entry (due 2026-11-22).
- Riley: update chat sample docs + fix model-compat table link (due 2026-11-21).
- Samira: pin tokenizers in samples/requirements.txt and add 3.11 test in samples CI (due 2026-11-25).
- Ava: draft a small "token-cost estimator" snippet + write blurb for privacy/data note (due 2026-12-02).

Outstanding questions / discussion points:
- Do we want samples to auto-detect private deployments and change help text? UX tradeoff: less confusion vs magic config.
- How opinionated should defaults be for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private? e.g., batching defaults, stream enabled/disabled.
- Can infra add a lightweight CI signal that runs every sample notebook headless and reports runtime/token counts? (Riley to check with infra).

Quick links to tickets / PRs we referenced:
- ENG-4921 (samples auth migration)
- ENG-4987 (samples CI 3.11 smoke)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/724 (example runtime test)
- Confluence draft: Quickstart Bootstrap (link in metadata)

Notes to self (unpolished):
- When we update quickstart page, add an "Instant try" section (single click run in collider/playground?). Quick wins increase conversion.
- Consider a small ribbon in the console that points new users at the 2-cell notebooks. Might require Console product buy-in.

Meeting end — left with a clear short sprint of work to de-risk samples and improve conversion. Will reconvene next Tues for PR reviews.
summary: short retro + concrete actions for bootstrap samples pilot. prioritized short-term fixes for auth, py3.11 pin, mini-embedding notebook, streaming hints + medium-term token-cost estimator and CI checklist.
